notes: A rerun of B1 on the Midflight of October 11, 2026 (S-11, S-12, and the connector fixes of that day), with the reviewer on Amazon Nova 2 Lite. Same prompts, same checks.
Midflight allows one project per repository, so this run reused B1's project: the old claims were withdrawn and the starting plan was approved again as plan v5. The plan change is plan v6.

A first attempt at phase 1 was discarded (kept as B2-aborted): four of five agents could not load Midflight's tools. The cause was a bug in the hosted service, fixed and deployed before this run (pull request #24). Nothing from that attempt is counted.

Phase 1: all five claims approved, nothing sent to the lead. Midflight recorded four assumptions as agreed between tasks, among them 'Reports (T4) will read bookings via a module-level BOOKINGS dict in app/bookings.py'. That seam is what failed in B1.
Phase 2: the lead approved plan v6 in Midflight; nothing was pasted to any agent. Directives went to T2, T3, T4, T5 and none to T1.

Phase 2: one escalation, E-27, the real disagreement (a 20% fee against a full refund), sent to the lead as a product question with both sides. T5's claim joined it. The lead resolved it once with the fixed decision, then sent messages 11 to 13.

After the decision, bookings stated how it would store the fee ('a cancelled booking keeps its original total and gains cancellation_fee and refunded') and named T4. Midflight recorded it as agreed (E-35). The question of what total holds, which needed a second escalation round in B1, never became a conflict.

Totals: 1 escalation, and it was real. No false alarm reached the lead or stopped an agent. The lead acted once after the plan approval. 7 assumptions recorded as agreed. Midflight settled no technical question itself, because none came up.
14 of 14 at merge, no fix round.

17 agent starts had Midflight connected but its tools not loaded; the driver restarted them before they did any work. The AWS account still allows only 10 simultaneous requests (an increase was requested during the run).
